info.title: CairnPost
info.description: CairnPost sends email through a mail provider and says what became of each one. Every call answers JSON unless it says otherwise, every time is UTC, and every error is one shape: a status, a `name` a program can switch on, and a `message` for a person. A request body with a field that is not described here is refused, never read in part. What a server limits (addresses, files, the size of a batch) is set by whoever runs it, so it is not written here. A path that takes another method answers 405 `method_not_allowed` with an `Allow` header, and a path that is no call answers 404 `route_not_found`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A name of your own for this request. The same request sent again under the same name is the same email and is answered as the first was, so a send whose answer was lost is safe to repeat.

409.description: The `Idempotency-Key` cannot be used this way now. `name` is one of: `invalid_idempotent_request`, `concurrent_idempotent_requests`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

422.description: The email is wrong as it stands, every address it names is suppressed, or the mail provider refused it for good. `name` is one of: `validation_error`, `recipient_suppressed`, `rejected_by_upstream`.

429.description: The mail provider's sending limit is reached. Nothing was sent. `name` is one of: `rate_limit_exceeded`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

502.description: The mail provider did not answer, so the email may or may not have gone. Send it again with the same `Idempotency-Key`. `name` is one of: `upstream_unknown`.

503.description: Nothing was sent. Try again later. `name` is one of: `unavailable`, `upstream_unavailable`, `schedule_full`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

post.description: Each is an email as `POST /emails` takes it. All are checked first, and one that could never be sent refuses the batch with nothing sent. After that the batch answers 200 or 207, never an error of one email's own. How many a batch may hold is set by the server. With an `Idempotency-Key` a batch is safe to send again as it was.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A name of your own for this request. The same request sent again under the same name is the same email and is answered as the first was, so a send whose answer was lost is safe to repeat.

200.description: The mail provider took every one. `data` says what became of each, in their order.

207.description: Some were not taken. `data` says what became of each, in their order. One that was not sent carries `error`, the answer it would have had alone, whose `name` is one of: `recipient_suppressed`, `rejected_by_upstream`, `invalid_idempotent_request`, `concurrent_idempotent_requests`, `rate_limit_exceeded`, `upstream_unavailable`, `upstream_unknown`, `schedule_full`, `not_started`, `unavailable`. The `Retry-After` header is the longest wait any of them asks for.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

503.description: The server is taking as many large emails as it can hold, or could not check the batch. Nothing was sent. `name` is one of: `unavailable`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

post.summary: Hand on an email that came
post.description: Called by whoever takes the sending domain's incoming mail, not by a client. It carries no API key: the headers are signed under the secret that side and this server both hold, and are checked before any of the email is read. The signature is `v1=` and the HMAC-SHA256, in hex, of the timestamp, the two addresses and the digest, each behind its length as eight bytes, big end first. A server with no inbound secret answers 404 `inbound_off`.

parameters.name: X-CairnPost-Timestamp
parameters.description: When it was handed on, in seconds since 1970.

parameters.name: X-CairnPost-To
parameters.description: The address it came for, as the sending server gave it. Whatever is not a printable ASCII character, and `%`, is written as `%` and two hex digits.

parameters.name: X-CairnPost-From
parameters.description: The address it came from, written the same way. Empty for a bounce.

parameters.name: X-CairnPost-Digest
parameters.description: The SHA-256 of the body, in hex.

parameters.name: X-CairnPost-Signature
parameters.description: The signature of the other four.

key.description: An API key: `Authorization: Bearer cp_...`. A call that asks for `admin` needs a key with the admin scope.

Unauthorized.description: No API key came with the request, or the key is not valid. `name` is one of: `missing_api_key`, `invalid_api_key`.

Forbidden.description: The key may not do this: the call needs an admin key, or the key is bound to another sending domain. `name` is one of: `admin_key_required`, `domain_not_allowed`.

NotFound.description: There is no such record. A path that is no call of the API answers `route_not_found`, which is not a missing record. `name` is one of: `not_found`, `route_not_found`.

Incomplete.description: The request body did not arrive whole in time. Nothing was done. `name` is one of: `request_incomplete`.

TooLarge.description: The request body is larger than the server takes. `name` is one of: `request_too_large`.

Invalid.description: The request is wrong as it stands and will not succeed if sent again unchanged. `message` says what to change. `name` is one of: `validation_error`.

Failed.description: Something went wrong in the server. `name` is one of: `internal_error`.

Unavailable.description: The server could not do it now. Nothing was done. Try again shortly. `name` is one of: `unavailable`.

name.description: What went wrong, as a name a program can switch on.

message.description: What went wrong and what to do, as a sentence for a person.

id.description: The email's id, when the send got far enough to have one. `GET /emails/{id}` says what became of it.

from.description: An email address, bare or with a name: `Ada <ada@example.com>`.

to.description: One address, or a list of them.

cc.description: One address, or a list of them.

bcc.description: One address, or a list of them.

headers.description: Headers of the email, by name.

scheduled_at.description: When to send it, as a time with its zone. Left out, it is sent now.

variables.description: What to fill the template's variables with, by name.

template.description: A template to make the email from, in place of `html` and `text`. The template's subject is used unless `subject` is given.

content_type.description: A media type. Left out, it is told from the filename's ending.

content_id.description: Give it one and the HTML can show the file: `` for `logo`.

attachments.description: Files to send with the email. How many and how large is set by the server.

SendEmail.description: One email. It needs `subject` and `html` or `text` or both, or a `template`, which gives all three. A field that is not listed here is refused, never dropped. How many addresses an email may name is set by the server.

suppressed.description: The addresses it was not sent to, being on the sending domain's suppression list. Left out when it went to all.

scheduled_at.description: When it will be sent, for an email that waits.

id.description: The email's id. An error can carry one too, as a send's does.

code.description: The receiving server's status, such as `5.1.1`.

reason.description: The mail provider's short name for what happened.

detail.description: The receiving server's own sentence. Shown under the rule for an email's content, since it can quote the email.

content_id.description: Set for a file the HTML shows.
